title: Trommel Screen

introduction.definition: A trommel is a rotating cylindrical or slightly conical screen. Material fed at the higher end tumbles inside the slowly turning drum; fines pass through the perforated shell and oversize leaves at the far end. The tumbling action breaks up lumps and frees fines, which makes trommels good for sticky or wet material.
key_points: Rotates at about 30–40 % of critical speed
Critical speed n_c ≈ 42.3 / √D (rpm, D in m)
introduction.summary: A trommel is a slowly rotating, slightly inclined perforated drum. Material tumbles along inside; small particles fall through the holes and oversize leaves at the far end. It handles sticky or wet material well and is common in compost, MSW, gold washing and mineral sizing.

foundation: Mount on a structure stiff enough that its natural frequencies are well away from the screen running speed (resonance check by the structural engineer).
alignment: Set the drum slope (typically a few degrees) and align trunnion rollers so the drum runs without axial thrust.
piping: Feed box/chute should spread the feed across the full width and drop it with low velocity; fit flexible dust seals between the vibrating body and fixed chutes.
Provide spray water headers for wet screening where needed.
commissioning: Run empty and measure stroke/amplitude and stroke angle (stroke card) at all four corners; check for rocking.
Check direction of rotation, bearing temperatures and the time to stop through resonance.

routine.task: Check for blinded holes and spillage.

periodic.task: Check trunnion wheels, tyres and drive.

overhaul.task: Replace screen panels and trunnion wheels.

lubrication: Trunnion and drive bearings greased; gearbox oil to schedule.

symptoms: Drum moves axially, wear on thrust rollers

safety: Guard trunnion and drive nips; lock out before entering the drum (confined space).

video_tutorials.title: Trommel Screen — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Trommel Screen.
A trommel is a rotating cylindrical or slightly conical screen.
Material fed at the higher end tumbles inside the slowly turning drum; fines pass through the perforated shell and oversize leaves at the far end.
The tumbling action breaks up lumps and frees fines, which makes trommels good for sticky or wet material.
Typical applications include compost, municipal waste and recycling; topsoil and sand/gravel; gold and alluvial mining (scrubbing); coal and ore desliming.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Rotating Perforated Drum with Riding Tyres & Girth Gear.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Trommel Screen.
Check for blinded holes and spillage.
Check trunnion wheels, tyres and drive.
Replace screen panels and trunnion wheels.
Watch for blinded apertures: fines in oversize. Common cause: wet clayey material, fibres wrapping.
Watch for drum wander/thrust: drum moves axially, wear on thrust rollers. Common cause: trunnion misalignment.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
